methods.signature: at(base: PlaneBase, offset: Num = 0, opts: PlaneOpts = {}): OffsetPlane
methods.summary: A workplane for a sketch: an offset plane, a face, a plane feature, a point and normal, or a tilt.
methods.description: at(base, offset, opts) returns a plane reference for sketch(). base is 'front' (moves along +Z), 'top' (+Y), 'right' (+X); a face(...) (the plane of that planar face, offset along its outward normal); a plane feature handle from part.workplane(...) + part.handle(); or { origin: [x,y,z], normal: [x,y,z], xdir? } for any plane (axis-aligned normals use a standard plane, others add three helper points and a three-point plane). opts.rotate = { axis: 'x'|'y'|'z' | edges(...), angle } tilts the plane about that line (the plane passes through the axis; an offset is applied before the rotation). A reference plane feature is added to the part.

parameters.name: base
parameters.description: 'front' | 'top' | 'right', face(sel), a plane feature handle, { origin, normal, xdir? }, or { between: [a, b] } (the mid plane of two planes or faces)

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: distance along the plane normal in mm (a number or expr), default 0

methods.notes:
- front moves along +Z, top along +Y, right along +X; a face offset goes along the face's OUTWARD normal (negative = into the body).
- { origin, normal } with a normal along a world axis is an ordinary offset plane; any other normal adds helper points and a three-point plane (7 features at most): fine for one-off tilted sketches, prefer rotate: { axis: 'x', angle } for a tilt about an axis.
- rotate turns the plane about the axis LINE, the plane passes through it; only world axes through the origin and straight edges are accepted.
- FRAME of { origin, normal, xdir }: the sketch origin is `origin`, sketch x (u) = xdir projected perpendicular to the normal, sketch y (v) = normal x u. Example: normal [1,0,0] with xdir [0,0,1] gives u = +Z and v = X x Z = -Y. Without xdir and with an axis-aligned normal the plane is the standard one (front / top / right frame below, a negative normal is flipped); without xdir and an oblique normal, u = normal x [1,0,0] (normal x [0,1,0] when the normal is nearly X). When a sketch lands in the wrong place, give xdir: it removes the guesswork.
- Standard frames (sketch x, sketch y, normal): front = X, Y, +Z; top = X, -Z, +Y; right = -Z, Y, +X. A point [u, v] on a plane offset by d is world = origin + u*x + v*y + d*normal.

methods.signature: .sketch(plane: Plane | OffsetPlane | PlaneRef | FaceSel, build: (s: SketchBuilder) => void, name?: string): this
methods.summary: Start a sketch on a plane or a face; the next extrude, cut or revolve uses it.
methods.description: Opens a sketch on 'front' (XY, normal +Z), 'top' (XZ, normal +Y), 'right' (ZY, normal +X), on at('front', 20) (a plane moved along its normal), or on a face(): face('>Z'). The callback draws with the sketch builder `s`. A feature needs its own sketch: each extrude / cut / revolve consumes the last sketch. Units mm, Y is up.

parameters.name: build
parameters.description: callback receiving the sketch builder s

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: optional name shown in the feature tree

methods.notes:
- A sketch on a face(): the sketch origin is the world origin projected on that face; coordinates are in mm.
- Feature order matters: sketch, then the feature that uses it. Two sketches in a row without a feature between them: only the last is used.
- Units mm, Y up. front = XY (normal +Z), top = XZ (normal +Y), right = ZY (normal +X).

methods.signature: .sketchFeature(on: Plane | OffsetPlane | FaceSel, json: { points: Array<Record<string, unknown>>; entities: Array<Record<string, unknown>>; constraints?: Array<Record<string, unknown>> })
methods.summary: Append a raw sketch (points, entities, constraints) on a plane.
methods.description: For sketches the builder cannot draw: pass the kernel's sketch JSON { points, entities, constraints? } and the plane ('front' | 'top' | 'right', at(plane, offset) or face(sel)). The next extrude, cut, revolve or rib consumes it. Point ids and entity ids are yours; remember the origin point O exists only if you declare it.

parameters.name: json
parameters.type: { points: Array<Record<string, unknown>>; entities: Array<Record<string, unknown>>; constraints?: Array<Record<string, unknown>> }
parameters.description: { points: [{ id, x, y }], entities: [{ id, type, ... }], constraints?: [] }

methods.example:
part('Tri').sketchFeature('front', { points: [{ id: 'a', x: 0, y: 0 }, { id: 'b', x: 20, y: 0 }, { id: 'c', x: 0, y: 20 }],
  entities: [{ id: 'e1', type: 'line', p1: 'a', p2: 'b' }, { id: 'e2', type: 'line', p1: 'b', p2: 'c' }, { id: 'e3', type: 'line', p1: 'c', p2: 'a' }] }).extrude(5);

methods.signature: .workplane(base: PlaneBase, offset: Num = 0, opts: PlaneOpts = {}): this
methods.summary: /** Add a reference plane (workplane) feature without a sketch.
methods.description: workplane(base, offset, opts) adds the plane that at() would add, as a feature of its own (visible in the tree, reusable): base is 'front' | 'top' | 'right', face(...), a plane handle, or { origin, normal, xdir? }; opts.rotate tilts it about an axis line. Take part.handle() right after it, then sketch(at(handle), ...) any number of times; at(handle, 5) offsets it further.

parameters.name: base
parameters.description: 'front' | 'top' | 'right', face(sel), a plane handle or { origin, normal, xdir? }

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: distance along the normal in mm, default 0

methods.notes:
- The plane frame is the one at() documents: for { origin, normal, xdir } sketch x = xdir (projected perpendicular to the normal), sketch y = normal x xdir, the origin is the sketch origin. Standard names: front = X, Y (normal +Z); top = X, -Z (normal +Y); right = -Z, Y (normal +X).
- Take part.handle() right after workplane() and sketch on at(handle). Planes are features: they show in the tree and survive edits.

methods.summary: The frame of a standard sketch plane: which world axes its sketch x, y and normal are.
methods.description: plane(name) returns { origin, x, y, normal, toWorld }. front: sketch x = world X, y = world Y, normal +Z. top: x = X, y = -Z (sketch y points to world -Z, so +sketch y is towards the back), normal +Y. right: x = -Z, y = Y, normal +X. Y is up. These come from the kernel's sketch frames; use toWorld([u, v], offset) to place a sketch point in the world, e.g. to aim a face selector or an expectBBox.
methods.notes: - Frames from the kernel: front x=X y=Y normal=+Z; top x=X y=-Z normal=+Y; right x=-Z y=Y normal=+X. So on 'top', sketch y grows towards world -Z; on 'right', sketch x grows towards world -Z.

methods.signature: s.arc(centre: Pt, start: Pt, end: Pt): this
methods.summary: Counter-clockwise arc about a centre from a start point to an end point.
methods.description: Adds an arc on the circle through `start` centred on `centre`, running counter-clockwise to `end` (projected on the radius). For an arc through three points in either direction use arc3.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: [x, y] where it ends (counter-clockwise from start)

methods.signature: s.arc3(a: Pt, m: Pt, b: Pt): this
methods.summary: Arc from a to b passing through the middle point m (either direction).
methods.description: Adds the arc of the circle through the three points. It fails if the points are in line. Easier than arc() when you know three points on the outline.

parameters.name: m
parameters.description: a point on the arc between a and b

methods.summary: Construction line along the sketch Y axis (the default revolve axis).
methods.description: revolve() adds this automatically when the sketch has no axis, so you rarely call it. Profile x is the distance from the axis, profile y the height along it.

methods.summary: Construction line used as the revolve axis when it is not the sketch Y axis.
methods.description: Adds a construction line between two sketch points and makes it the axis of the next revolve. Normally you pass the same thing as revolve(360, { axis: { from, to } }), which calls this for you.

methods.summary: Circle given its RADIUS (not diameter).
methods.description: Adds a circle of radius r centred on `at`. Remember radius: a 10 mm bore is circle(5). Several circles in one sketch with nesting make rings; a circle on a face with cut() makes a round pocket or a through bore.
methods.notes:
- RADIUS, not diameter: a 10 mm bore is circle(5).
- To drill, prefer part.hole / holes.* over a circle + cut: they carry the hole kind and are one feature.

methods.signature: s.curve(f: (t: number) => Pt, o: { from?: number; to?: number; count?: number; closed?: boolean; t0?: number; t1?: number; n?: number } = {})
methods.summary: Curve from a JavaScript function t -> [x, y], sampled into a fitted spline.
methods.description: s.curve((t) => [x, y], { from: 0, to: 1, count: 48, closed: false }) calls the function at count equal steps of t from `from` to `to` and draws one interpolating spline through the points (units: mm, JS maths: sin and cos take radians). Open (the default): count + 1 points, the last at t = to. closed: true makes a full loop WITHOUT repeating the end point: t runs from `from` up to but not including `to` (so for a circle use from 0, to 2 * Math.PI), count points, and the spline closes on itself, which is what a loft section or an extrude profile needs. The function may use the script's variables and any JS; it is sampled when the script runs, so for a curve the kernel should keep as formulas (editable, refitted to a tolerance) use s.equation. Fewer than 3 points, a function that does not return two finite numbers, or count above 2000 stops the run with the line. Defaults: from 0, to 1, count 48, points rounded to 0.0001 mm.

parameters.name: o
parameters.type: { from?: number; to?: number; count?: number; closed?: boolean; t0?: number; t1?: number; n?: number }

properties.name: from
properties.description: first t, default 0

properties.name: to
properties.description: last t (excluded when closed), default 1

properties.name: count
properties.description: number of steps, default 48 (alias n; from / to are also t0 / t1)

properties.name: closed
properties.description: close the curve into a loop, default false

methods.example:
// a closed loft section: an egg shape, 60 points
part('Egg').sketch('front', (s) => s.curve((a) => [20 * Math.cos(a), 26 * Math.sin(a) * (1 + 0.15 * Math.cos(a))], { from: 0, to: 2 * Math.PI, count: 60, closed: true })).extrude(8);

methods.signature: s.cvspline(pts: Pt[], o: { closed?: boolean; degree?: number } = {})
methods.summary: Control-vertex spline: the points are the control polygon, not on the curve.
methods.description: Adds a B-spline whose control vertices are the points (the curve is pulled towards them but does not pass through). Degree 3 by default. Use it for fair, smooth outlines where overshoot of an interpolating spline is a problem. closed: true makes a periodic loop.

parameters.name: pts
parameters.description: control points [x, y], at least degree + 1

properties.name: closed
properties.description: close the curve into a loop

properties.name: degree
properties.description: curve degree, default 3

methods.signature: s.equation(o: { x: string; y: string; t: [Num | string, Num | string]; tol?: number; name?: string }): this
methods.summary: Curve from formulas x(t), y(t): the kernel fits a spline with the fewest points within the tolerance.
methods.description: Adds a spline entity that stores the formulas; the kernel evaluates them on every rebuild, so a curve written with variables follows them. Formulas use the expression syntax of dimensions: + - * / ^, sqrt sin cos tan abs, min max pow mod hypot atan2 round floor ceil exp ln log10 asin acos atan, pi; TRIGONOMETRY IS IN DEGREES (a full turn is t from 0 to 360); any name other than t must be a declared variable. `t` is [start, end] (numbers, expr(), or formula strings); `tol` is the largest distance in mm from the formulas (default 0.01). A curve that ends where it starts is closed (a region of its own); an open one needs lines to close it, starting and ending exactly at the curve's end points (compute them from the formulas). Errors name the formula (equationFormula, equationNotFinite, equationRange, equationTolerance, equationDegenerate); a curve that crosses itself warns equationSelfIntersects. `name` sets the entity id; its points are <name>_start, <name>_p1.., <name>_end.

parameters.name: o
parameters.type: { x: string; y: string; t: [Num | string, Num | string]; tol?: number; name?: string }
parameters.description: { x: formula of t, y: formula of t, t: [start, end], tol?: mm, name? }

methods.signature: s.grid(origin: Pt, pitch: Pt, count: [number, number]): this
methods.summary: Points on a rectangular grid.
methods.description: Adds nx by ny points starting at `origin` with spacing `pitch` along x then y (x varies fastest).

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: [nx, ny] number of points along x and y

methods.summary: One line segment between two points.
methods.description: Adds a single line from a to b. Combine with arc or arc3 to close a profile that has curved sides (a half disc is arc3 plus a line).

methods.summary: Offset the chain drawn last.
methods.description: Offsets the connected chain that contains the most recently drawn entity: lines and arcs joined end to end (the chain stops at a point where three or more meet), a circle, or one fit-point spline. Corners are re-joined at the intersection of the offset lines, arcs keep their centre and change radius, and a segment that would collapse is dropped. Use it for wall thickness: draw the outside once, offset it for the inside, and no coordinate is calculated by hand. SIGN: for an OPEN chain a positive distance is to the LEFT of the direction of travel (the order the points were given in; walking east, left is +y, towards the top of the sketch), negative to the right. For a CLOSED loop or a circle positive is OUTWARD and negative inward, whichever way it was drawn. The chain drawn before stays unless keep: false (the offset replaces it). The ends of an open chain move along the normal of their end segments; close the profile with your own lines at the known end coordinates. Draw only the chain to offset before the call, and the closing lines after it.

parameters.name: distance
parameters.description: signed offset in mm (see SIGN above), not zero

properties.name: keep
properties.description: keep the original chain next to its copy (default true); false replaces it with the copy

methods.example: part('Cup').sketch('front', (s) => { s.polyline([[0, 0], [20, 0], [20, 40]]); s.offset(-2, { keep: false }); s.polyline([[18, 38], [0, 38]]).polyline([[0, 38], [0, 2]]); }).revolve(360, { axis: { from: [0, 0], to: [0, 1] } });

methods.summary: A single point (a hole centre).
methods.description: Adds a point entity. Points in a sketch are used as hole centres by hole features; for a hole use part.hole or part.holes.* rather than placing points yourself.

methods.summary: Several points (hole centres).
methods.description: Adds one point entity per [x, y]. See holes.points for the usual way to drill them.

methods.signature: s.polar(count: number | ((angle: number) => number), draw?: ((s: SketchBuilder) => void) | { count?: number; closed?: boolean; from?: number; to?: number; center?: Pt }, o: { about?: Pt; angle?: number; start?: number } = {})
methods.summary: Repeat a drawing around a centre.
methods.description: polar(count, draw) runs `draw(s)` count times; copy i is rotated by i * 360 / count degrees about `about` (default the sketch origin). Draw the first copy where you want it and write the shapes once: a petal, a spoke, a tooth. The copies are separate loops, so a sketch with five petals extrudes or cuts as five regions. angle spreads the copies over a part of a turn instead (angle: 90 with count 4 gives 0, 30, 60 and 90 degrees), start turns the first copy.

parameters.name: draw
parameters.type: ((s: SketchBuilder) => void) | { count?: number; closed?: boolean; from?: number; to?: number; center?: Pt }
parameters.description: function that draws one copy with the same sketch builder

parameters.name: o
parameters.type: { about?: Pt; angle?: number; start?: number }

properties.name: about
properties.description: centre of rotation [x, y] (default [0, 0])

properties.name: angle
properties.description: total angle the copies span (default 360, copies evenly around the circle)

properties.name: start
properties.description: rotation of the first copy in degrees (default 0)

methods.signature: s.polarCurve(f: (angle: number) => number, o: { count?: number; n?: number; closed?: boolean; from?: number; to?: number; center?: Pt } = {})
methods.summary: Polar curve from a function angle -> radius (waves, cams, petals).
methods.description: Call it as s.polar((angle) => radius, o), the same as s.polarCurve: waves, cams, petals, rounded stars. s.polar((angle) => radius, { count: 96, closed: true }) draws r(angle) round the sketch origin (or `center`) as one interpolating spline. The angle is in RADIANS (JS Math.sin / Math.cos), measured from the sketch x axis counter-clockwise, from 0 to 2 * Math.PI by default; closed: true (the default for a full turn) makes a loop without repeating the end point, ready to extrude or to use as a loft section. Give from / to for a sector (open spline, closed: false). The radius must be a finite number (negative values draw on the opposite side). count defaults to 96 points: use about 8 points per wave of the function, more for sharp features; the spline passes through the points, so a coarse count rounds corners. Points are rounded to 0.0001 mm. Use sketch.curve for anything that is not a radius against an angle.

parameters.name: f
parameters.description: function of the angle in radians returning the radius in mm

parameters.name: o
parameters.type: { count?: number; n?: number; closed?: boolean; from?: number; to?: number; center?: Pt }

properties.name: count
properties.description: number of points, default 96 (alias n)

properties.name: closed
properties.description: close the loop, default true for a full turn and false when from / to are given

properties.name: from
properties.description: first angle in radians, default 0

properties.name: to
properties.description: last angle in radians (excluded when closed), default 2 * Math.PI

properties.name: center
properties.description: [x, y] centre, default [0, 0]

methods.example:
// a wavy disc outline: radius 30 with 12 waves 3 mm deep
part('Wavy').sketch('front', (s) => s.polar((a) => 30 + 1.5 * Math.cos(12 * a), { count: 120 })).extrude(5);

methods.signature: s.polarPoints(center: Pt, radius: number, n: number, startAngle: number = 0): this
methods.summary: Points on a circle: a bolt circle of centres.
methods.description: Adds `n` points on a circle of `radius` about `center`, the first at `startAngle` degrees (counter-clockwise from sketch x). For drilled holes use part.holes.polar.

methods.summary: Closed polygon through the points.
methods.description: Adds a closed profile of straight lines through the points, in order; the last point joins the first. Coordinates are in the sketch plane in mm. Use it for L, T, U shapes and for revolve profiles (half cross-section).

parameters.name: pts
parameters.description: list of [x, y] points, at least three

methods.notes:
- Points go in order around the profile, either direction; the shape closes itself.
- For a revolve profile keep every x >= 0 (radius).

methods.summary: Open chain of lines through the points.
methods.description: Adds line segments joining consecutive points without closing. An open chain extrudes only when thin walls are requested (thin option) or when it is closed by other entities of the same sketch.

methods.signature: s.rect(w: Num, h: Num, at: Pt = [0, 0]): this
methods.summary: Rectangle of width x height centred on a point.
methods.description: Adds a closed rectangle: width along sketch x, height along sketch y, centred on `at` (default the sketch origin). A second rect inside the first makes a frame (ring) that extrudes as a hollow section.

methods.signature: s.rrect(w: Num, h: Num, r: Num, at: Pt = [0, 0]): this
methods.summary: Rounded rectangle: width x height with corner radius r.
methods.description: Adds four lines and four arcs that share end points, centred on `at`. With r <= 0 it is a plain rect. Prefer this over filleting the vertical edges of a plate afterwards: it is faster and more robust.

methods.summary: Interpolating spline: a smooth curve through the points.
methods.description: Adds a spline that passes through every point (a fit-point spline). closed: true makes it a closed loop through the points (a profile you can extrude); open splines are paths for sweep or lofts guides, or edges of an outline with other entities.

parameters.name: pts
parameters.description: list of [x, y] points the curve passes through, at least 3 (2 for an open one)

properties.name: closed
properties.description: close the curve into a loop

methods.notes: - Fit-point spline: the curve passes through the points. closed: true makes a loop (extrudable and a loft section), open splines are sweep paths. Many points on a tight turn can overshoot; cvspline gives a fairer curve from control points.

methods.signature: s.text(string: string, at: Pt | { x: number; y: number }, opts: TextOpts = {}): this
methods.summary: Lettering: the outlines of a string as closed regions (engrave it with cut, emboss it with extrude).
methods.description: Adds a `text` entity: the letters of a built-in font become closed loops that extrude and cut like any sketch profile, so ENGRAVE = sketch on the face + cut(0.3), EMBOSS = sketch + extrude(0.3). `at` is the anchor [x, y] (or {x, y}); `height` is the CAP height in mm (the height of an H, default 5); fonts: 'gauge' (condensed sans, default) and 'engrave' (serif), or the id of a library font ('barlow', 'source-sans-3', 'barlow-condensed', 'bebas-neue', 'pt-serif', 'special-elite', 'ibm-plex-mono', 'great-vibes', 'satisfy', 'anton': the app loads it, nothing else to do; no kerning or ligatures; overlapping strokes of a font may fail to engrave); anchor is [horizontal, vertical] = 'left'|'center'|'right' x 'baseline'|'middle'|'top' (or one string 'center middle'), default left baseline, measured on the ink box; angle in degrees counter-clockwise about the anchor; spacing scales the letter pitch (default 1); mirror flips the text (for the back of a clear part); arc: { centre: [x, y], radius, angleCentre (deg, default 90), side: 'outside' (tops away from the centre, reads clockwise) | 'inside' (tops toward the centre, reads counter-clockwise) } lays the letters along a circle (radius is the baseline). KEEP LETTERING IN A SKETCH OF ITS OWN (its loops are not intersected with other curves of the sketch); several text() calls in one sketch are fine (dial numerals). Text under 0.8 mm cap height warns textTooSmall; characters outside Latin-1 are skipped (textMissingGlyph). `name` sets the entity id (letters, digits, - and _), which shows in the sketch's inspect `texts`. Use await part.textMetrics(string, opts) to size a plate or centre by the real width.

parameters.name: string
parameters.description: the text (1 to 500 characters, one line)

parameters.name: at
parameters.description: anchor [x, y] or {x, y} in the sketch plane, mm

parameters.name: opts
parameters.description: { font: 'gauge'|'engrave'|library id (see above), height, anchor, angle, spacing, mirror, arc, polyline, name }

properties.name: arc
properties.type: { centre?: Pt; radius: Num; angleCentre?: Num; side?: 'outside' | 'inside' }

methods.example:
part('Plate').sketch('front', (s) => s.rect(60, 20)).extrude(4)
  .sketch(at('front', 4), (s) => s.text('SEA SPRITE', [0, 0], { font: 'engrave', height: 5, anchor: ['center', 'middle'] })).cut(0.3);
methods.notes:
- Put lettering in a sketch of ITS OWN: its loops are not intersected with the other curves of the sketch (letters inside a rect do not become holes of it). Several s.text() calls in one sketch are fine (dial numerals).
- height is the CAP height (an H), not the font size; under 0.8 mm the run warns textTooSmall. Engrave 0.1 to 0.5 mm deep: cut(0.3). Emboss = extrude(0.15).
- Upright numerals around a dial: one text per number, anchor ['center', 'middle'], angle 0, at the numeral radius; the arc option bends ONE string along a circle (side 'outside' reads clockwise over the top, 'inside' with angleCentre 270 reads left to right below).
- Keep letters clear of other thin features (ridges, tick marks): a glyph corner touching a ridge corner can make the kernel boolean fail (booleanFailed); move the numeral radius by a few tenths of a mm if it does.
- Characters outside Latin-1 are skipped with a textMissingGlyph warning; an empty or blank string is an error.
- Fonts: 'gauge' and 'engrave' are built in; a library font is named by its id ('barlow', 'bebas-neue', 'great-vibes' ...) and loaded by the app. Library fonts have no kerning or ligatures; connected script faces (great-vibes, satisfy) and some display faces have overlapping strokes that can make an engrave fail validation or warn textOverlappingContours; keep those strings short. An unknown id lists the valid ones.

methods.summary: A ball bearing as separate bodies (rings, balls when open), placed by an origin and an axis.
methods.description: The free-function form of the bearing method: bearing({ designation: '608', seal: '2RS' }) adds a bearing to the current part (a new one when there is none) and returns it. Give a preset designation ('608', '6204', 'MR63', 'R2') or bore, od and width in mm. seal is '2Z' (default), '2RS' or 'open' (visible balls). origin is the centre of the first face and axis the way the bearing extends from it (default [0, 0, 1]). Each ring and ball is its own body.

methods.signature: .baseFlange(o: { rule?: string; flip?: boolean; regions?: unknown[] } = {})
methods.summary: Sheet base plate from the last closed sketch.
methods.description: Adds a baseFlange from the last sketch (which it consumes, as extrude does). The sketch must hold ONE closed outline (holes inside it are allowed); the sheet extends along the sketch normal (against it with flip), the sketch plane is the front face and the opposite face the back (cap) face. methods.summary: A ball bearing as separate bodies: two rings (with shields or seals) and, when open, the balls.
methods.description: Give a preset designation ('608', '6204', 'MR63', 'R2' for a 1/8 inch bore) or bore, od and width in mm; the presets are the nominal ISO 15 sizes of the miniature 6xx, MR, 60xx, 62xx and 63xx series and some inch sizes. seal: '2Z' (default) is a flat shield disc on both faces, '2RS' a thicker seal with a sloping lip, 'open' shows the balls (count and diameter from the race gap, or balls and ballDiameter). All four corners of each ring are chamfered (chamfer, default by size). Each race has a ball groove (an arc about the ball centre circle, radius 0.52 ball diameters, 0.27 deep; a plain race when the bearing is too small for one), no cage, so this is for assemblies, fit checks and looks, not for load ratings. origin is the centre of the first face and axis the way the bearing extends from it (default [0, 0, 1]). Each ring and ball is its own body and does not merge with what it touches. onFace: 'F2.C1' builds the bearing from that face instead of from absolute numbers (the origin must lie on the face and the axis point into the part along x, y or z), so a later edit that moves the face moves the bearing and its pocket with it. seat: true first cuts a pocket for the outer ring into the bodies that exist (diameter with an H7 housing allowance, depth the width), seat: { fit: 'press' | 'h7' | 'print', allowance } picks another fit.

methods.summary: Cut the last sketch out of the body: a depth or through().
methods.description: Removes material. direction: 'into' (the kernel default: AGAINST the sketch normal, which is into the body from a face sketch), 'away' (along the normal), 'both' (symmetric about the sketch plane; depth is the total) or 'auto' (the default for cuts: try 'into'; if the kernel reports cutNoEffect because the body is on the other side, flip once and add the warning 'cut direction flipped automatically'). Give direction explicitly to avoid the extra build. Depth is a number or through() for all the way. Same other options as extrude (mid, flip, draft, thin). A cut changes EVERY body it reaches; from: 'Name' (or a list) limits it to the bodies of that name (made with newBody: 'Name'), so no separate cutter body and combine are needed: an unknown name is an error that lists the bodies the part has.

properties.name: from
properties.description: body name or list of names the cut changes (default: every body it reaches)

properties.name: mid
properties.description: cut half each way

properties.name: flip
properties.description: reverse direction

properties.name: draft
properties.description: taper angle in degrees

properties.name: direction
properties.description: 'auto' (default: into, flip once if nothing is cut) | 'into' | 'away' | 'both'

methods.notes:
- Direction is relative to the SKETCH NORMAL: 'into' = against it (the kernel's default for a cut, into the body from a face sketch), 'away' = along it, 'both' = symmetric about the sketch plane (depth is the total). The default is 'auto': try 'into'; if the kernel says cutNoEffect, flip once and add the warning 'cut direction flipped automatically'. Pass the direction yourself to skip the retry.
- front/top/right normals are +Z/+Y/+X: a cut sketched on 'front' at z = 0 with the body above it (z > 0) is 'away'.
- A cut sketch must overlap the material in plan; a circle outside the body gives `cutNoEffect` in BOTH directions (the auto flip does not hide it).
- Several shapes in ONE sketch are ONE cut feature (draw pockets in a loop, then cut once).
- Depth beyond the body is fine; through() is clearer when you mean all the way.
- A cut applies to EVERY body that exists when it runs (not only the one you are looking at). A through-cut for holes in a base plate also slits any earlier body it crosses. Build the parts the cut must not touch AFTER the cut, or keep clearance, or limit the cut depth. run_script reports a warning ('cut F7 changed N bodies') when one cut changed several bodies.

On the panel tree any panel takes a flange: 'P2.tip' (free end of leg 2), 'P1.side.start', { edge: n, panel: k }. A point on the cap (back) face bends the flange towards the cap (direction up in the bend table), a point on the front face bends it the other way; flip reverses. Object picks may carry their own height, angle, radius, heightFrom, position and flip. height is measured from heightFrom (outer virtual sharp by default); it must reach the end of the bend (flangeHeightTooLow otherwise). Several edges in one call stay `gap` apart at the corners. then chains further bends on the far edge of the leg.

methods.summary: Extrude the last sketch into a solid (adds material).
methods.description: Extrudes the last sketch along its plane normal by `depth` mm. Options: direction ('away' = along the sketch normal, the default; 'into' = against it; 'both' = symmetric about the plane, depth is the total, same as mid), flip (the old way to reverse), draft (taper angle in degrees), thin (hollow wall thickness: closed profile gives a tube, open profile a thin sheet). Sketch normals: front +Z, top +Y, right +X (see plane()); a face sketch's normal points out of the body. The first extrude makes the body; later ones add to it (a boss when sketched on a face).

properties.name: newBody
properties.description: true or 'Name': keep the solid as a separate body instead of fusing it with what it touches or overlaps

properties.name: mid
properties.description: extrude half each way (same as direction: 'both'; symmetric: true is the same)

properties.name: flip
properties.description: reverse direction

properties.name: draft
properties.description: taper angle in degrees

properties.name: thin
properties.description: wall thickness for a thin-walled extrude (centred on the profile), or { thickness, side: 'inside' | 'outside' | 'mid' | 'both', thickness2, ends, cornerStyle }: the same options as the thin-wall card (the card starts at 'inside', a plain number here is 'mid')

properties.name: direction
properties.description: 'away' (along the sketch normal, default) | 'into' (against it) | 'both' (symmetric, depth is the total)

methods.notes:
- Each extrude consumes the sketch before it: sketch again for the next feature.
- A sketch on a face adds material outward (a boss). On the 'front' plane it goes +Z, on 'top' +Y, on 'right' +X; direction 'into' reverses, 'both' (or mid) is symmetric with depth as the total.
- On the 'top' and 'right' planes the sketch axes are not x/y of the world (top: sketch y = world -Z; right: sketch x = world -Z); see plane() for the table.
- Nested closed shapes in one sketch (rect inside rect) give a ring, not two solids.
- draft is in degrees and tapers the sides inward for a positive angle on a boss.
- Touching or overlapping solids FUSE into one body. To keep a solid separate pass { newBody: true } or { newBody: 'Name' } (extrude, revolve and sweep; not for cuts). Two newBody solids may overlap without merging; leave a clearance (0.1 mm) between parts that must not fuse and use the bodies tool to check the body count.

Use it for types like draft, helix, lip, dome or moveFace; prefer the typed helpers when one exists. Field names are the kernel's (docs/spec-agent-interface.md).

parameters.description: the feature object, e.g. { type: 'shell', faces: [face('>Z')], thickness: 2 }

- Escape hatch for kernel types without a helper (draft, helix, lip, dome, moveFace, ...). The type is checked against the kernel's list; field names are the kernel's, see docs/spec-agent-interface.md.

methods.signature: .fillet(on: EdgeSel, radius: Num | { name?: string; radius?: Num | Num[] | Record<string, Num>; variable?: [Num, Num] }): this
methods.summary: Round edges: one radius, a radius per edge, or a variable radius.
methods.description: Rounds the edges chosen by edges(). radius is a number (constant), or an options object: { radius: number | number[] | {[edgeKey]: number} } where an array gives one radius per selected edge in selection order (its length must equal the edge count) and an object maps edge keys (like 'F2.C0|F2.S.l1#0', as listed by part.edges... or '*' for the rest) to radii; edges with different radii become one fillet feature per distinct radius, applied in order of increasing radius (so a sequence of fillets, not one simultaneous blend: edges that meet at a vertex can fail with blendOverflow, then give them the same radius). { variable: [near, far] } makes ONE fillet whose radius changes linearly along each selected edge from the end nearer the start to the far end. Fails when a radius is too big for the adjacent faces (blendOverflow). Fillet before shelling and before adding small features; select with edges('|Z') for the vertical edges of a block.

parameters.name: radius
parameters.type: Num | { name?: string; radius?: Num | Num[] | Record<string, Num>; variable?: [Num, Num] }
parameters.description: radius in mm (number or expr), or { radius, variable }

methods.notes:
- A radius that is too big for the neighbouring faces gives `blendOverflow`: halve it. Radius equal to half a face width is already a limit.
- Fillet before shell and before small holes; fillet edges('|Z') for the vertical edges of a block, or draw sketch.rrect instead.
- A fillet selected by edges() of faces that do not exist yet fails with a Line N selector error: select at the point in the chain where the edge exists.
- Different radii on edges that meet at a corner are applied as SEQUENTIAL fillets (one per distinct radius, increasing) and can fail with blendFailed where a simultaneous blend would not; use one radius there, or fillet the corners in a sketch (rrect).
- { variable: [near, far] } works on isolated edges; edge junctions (all four edges of a face) fail with blendFailed.

methods.summary: Knurl a cylinder: cut straight, diamond or pyramid grooves into it.
methods.description: Describe the cylinder (axis x, y or z, centre, radius, axial range from..to). 'straight' cuts axial grooves in one cut (fast). 'diamond' cuts two crossed helical sets, one per hand, each a twisted sweep (slow: the helper stops above 260 groove crossings, count squared times twice the turn fraction, because the kernel's boolean budget fails around 570). 'pyramid' crosses axial grooves with rings for raised square pyramids. Give count (per hand for a diamond) or pitch, and depth (default pitch / 4). profile 'v' (angle, default 90) or 'round' (width, default 2 * depth). mode 'cosmetic' skips the cutting: it records the knurl in the document for display only, instant at any count. Overlapping grooves are refused with the largest count that fits. On a 20 mm diameter, 12 mm band: straight 24 grooves under 1 s, pyramid 24 x 8 about 11 s, diamond 12 + 12 at 22 degrees about 4 s, 16 + 16 at 45 degrees about 23 s. onFace: { face: 'F2.C1', at: 30 } builds the cut grooves from that end face of the cylinder (a flat face whose normal lies along the axis; `at` is where it is) instead of from the numbers from and to, which then only say where the band lies at the moment: change the length of the shaft and the band keeps its distance from the face. Diamond and pyramid need method: 'boolean' for it (the faceted band is one feature with fixed numbers). faceted (the default for a V diamond or pyramid) builds the surface as faces in the kernel: linear in the groove count, planar flanks (volume within about 3 percent); method 'boolean' cuts the grooves one set against the other (slow when dense; round grooves and straight always use the cuts).

parameters.name: o
parameters.description: options object { radius, from, to, count | pitch, ... }, the fields below

part('Knob').sketch('front', (s) => s.circle(15)).extrude(12)
  .knurl({ axis: 'z', radius: 15, from: 0, to: 12, pattern: 'straight', count: 36, depth: 0.5 });

Sections are { on, draw } where draw(s) draws a closed outline with the sketch builder, or { on, point: [x, y] } for a single-point section. Only the FIRST and the LAST section may be a point (a bow, a cone tip); ends.first / ends.last say 'cap' (flat end, default) or 'point' and are checked against the sections. Optional guides are sketches the loft follows, centre is a straight centre-line sketch, startNormal / endNormal (true or a tension number) make the loft leave the end sections along their normals. Closed (ring) lofts are not supported by the kernel. Section outlines should have the same number of pieces and be simple closed curves; a hull is a row of arcs or polygons with growing size.

parameters.description: list of section sketches, at least two, in order

parameters.name: o
parameters.type: { ends?: { first?: End; last?: End }; guides?: SketchSpec[]; centre?: SketchSpec; startNormal?: boolean | Num; endNormal?: boolean | Num; op?: 'add' | 'cut'; from?: string | string[]; newBody?: boolean | string }

properties.description: { first?: 'cap' | 'point', last?: 'cap' | 'point' }

properties.name: guides
properties.description: guide curve sketches ({ on, draw }) that touch every section

properties.name: centre
properties.description: centre-line sketch ({ on, draw }) with a straight line

properties.description: true or a tension: leave the first section along its normal

properties.name: endNormal
properties.description: true or a tension: arrive at the last section along its normal

properties.name: op

- Sections are { on, draw } objects, not previously recorded sketches: loft() builds the sketches itself. Put the sections on parallel planes with at('right', x) (stations along X), at('front', z) (along Z) or at('top', y). On 'right' the sketch x axis points to -Z and y is up.
- Same outline kind in every section (all splines, or all arc+line pieces); a closed spline per station is the robust hull recipe (boat-hull-loft).
- A point end is { on, point: [x, y] } with ends: { last: 'point' }: first OR last, never both and never in the middle; no guides with a point end. A point in the middle is a script error with the line number.
- The result is checked by the kernel: a self-crossing section is loftProfileSelfIntersect, a degenerate result loftInvalidResult. Fix the section, not the loft.
- No closed (ring) loft in the kernel. Guides must touch every section (loftGuideMiss); a centre line must run through the sections (loftCentreLineReach: it runs along the loft axis, mind the direction of the plane axes).

methods.summary: Refold an unfolded sheet.
methods.description: Adds a refold directly after an unfold; it rebuilds the folded solid from the bend table, so unfold and refold round-trip exactly (volume, faces, box). A refold of a sheet that is not unfolded is refused (sheetMetalUnsupported).

methods.signature: .revolve(angle: Num = 360, o: { name?: string; op?: 'add' | 'cut'; thin?: ThinOpt; axis?: { from: Pt; to: Pt }; newBody?: boolean | string; from?: string | string[] } = {}): this
methods.summary: Revolve the last sketch about an axis (lathe parts: pulleys, bushings, flanges).
methods.description: Revolves the last sketch `angle` degrees (default 360). The axis is the sketch Y axis unless axis: { from, to } gives a line in the sketch plane. Profile x is the radius, y the height along the axis, so draw a half cross-section on one side of the axis. op: 'cut' removes the revolved volume instead. thin makes a revolved shell.

parameters.name: o
parameters.type: { name?: string; op?: 'add' | 'cut'; thin?: ThinOpt; axis?: { from: Pt; to: Pt }; newBody?: boolean | string; from?: string | string[] }

properties.name: op
properties.description: add (default) or cut

properties.name: thin
properties.description: wall thickness for a thin revolve (centred on the profile), or { thickness, side: 'inside' | 'outside' | 'mid' | 'both', thickness2 }: 'inside' grows the wall to the LEFT of the profile's direction of travel (the inside of a bend), 'outside' to the right, 'mid' (default) centres it; draw the profile the other way round to swap. A centred wall that would cross the axis (profileCrossesAxis) needs 'inside' or 'outside'

properties.name: axis
properties.description: { from: [x, y], to: [x, y] } axis line in the sketch plane

properties.name: newBody
properties.description: true or 'Name': keep the solid as a separate body instead of fusing it with what it touches or overlaps

properties.name: from
properties.description: with op 'cut': a body name or list of names (bodies made with newBody) the cut changes; the other bodies stay as they are

methods.notes:
- Draw the half profile on ONE side of the axis: x is the distance from the axis, y the height. Keep the profile from crossing the axis (no negative x).
- The sketch plane decides the world axis: on 'front' and 'right' the sketch Y axis is world Y or world Z accordingly; for a pulley on 'right' the axis is world Y and the end faces are face('>Y') / face('<Y').
- 360 is a full solid of revolution; a smaller angle leaves two planar end faces.
- A profile that crosses the axis (points on both sides of the revolve axis) gives profileCrossesAxis. Draw HALF of the profile, from the axis outwards (x >= 0), and let the 360 degrees make the other side.

methods.summary: Rib: a web of a given thickness from an open sketch line, grown to the body.
methods.description: Takes the LAST sketch, an open line or chain (not closed), and adds a web of this total thickness centred on the sketch plane. The web fills the space between the chain and the body on the side the body encloses: a gusset across the inside corner of an L, a web inside a box. A line in open air, or one that does not have material around it, fails with ribNoContact. The chain ends may touch or lie inside the material. flip tries the other side first.

properties.name: flip
properties.description: try the other side of the chain first

methods.notes:
- The sketch is an OPEN line or chain (a closed outline is ribNeedsOpenSketch) and it must have material enclosing the space between the chain and the body, such as the inside corner of an L or a pocket: a line across open air fails with ribNoContact.
- The web is centred on the sketch plane, so put the sketch on the plane of the rib's mid-section (at('front', z)).

methods.summary: A screw or bolt as its own body: head, drive and shank, placed by an origin and an axis.
methods.description: Give the metric size (M2 to M16; M12 and M16 have button, countersunk and hex heads only, as the standards stop there) and the shank length; head and drive sizes come from an ISO table and can be overridden. head: 'pan' (default), 'button', 'countersunk', 'cheese' or 'hex'. drive: 'slotted', 'hex' (socket), 'cross', 'torx' or 'none'. Cross is an approximation (two tapered wings with a small flat tip) and so is torx: fine for looks, fit checks and mass. origin is the centre of the bearing face and axis is the way the shank points (default [0, 0, -1]). The screw is its own body and does not merge with what it touches. thread: true is refused for now.

parameters.name: o
parameters.description: options object { size, length, head, drive, origin, axis, ... }, the fields below

methods.example:
part('Plate').sketch('front', (s) => s.rect(30, 30)).extrude(4).hole(face('>Z'), [0, 0], { diameter: 3.4 })
  .screw({ size: 'M3', length: 8, head: 'button', drive: 'hex', origin: [0, 0, 4] });

methods.summary: Turn a bent-plate solid into a sheet metal part.
methods.description: Adds a sheetConvert: the solid (planar panels, straight cylindrical bends, constant thickness) becomes a sheet with a panel tree, flat pattern and bend table, so edgeFlange, fold, sheetCut, sheet_info and sheet_export work on it. thickness is read from the body unless given; rule names the rule that supplies the k-factor (the converted rule is named Converted and becomes active). Refused with sheetMetalUnsupported for sharp corners between panels, cones, tori, free-form bends, reliefs or embossed features (the rebuilt sheet must match the volume within 1 %).

properties.name: thickness
properties.description: sheet thickness in mm (default: read from the body)

properties.name: rule
properties.description: name of a sheetRules rule for the k-factor (default: the active rule)

methods.signature: .sheetCorner(corners: SheetCorner | SheetCorner[], o: { mode?: 'round' | 'chamfer'; radius?: Num | string; distance?: Num | string; size?: Num | string } = {})
methods.summary: Round or chamfer free convex corners of the sheet.
methods.description: Adds a sheetCorner. corners are world points (the nearest panel vertex wins) or { panel: k, vertex: i }. mode is 'round' (default, needs radius) or 'chamfer' (needs distance); size works for either. Both walls of the corner must be free (no bend beside them), the corner convex, and the walls at least as long as the tangent length. The fillet is a cylinder face in the solid and an arc in the DXF.

parameters.name: corners
parameters.description: a corner or a list: [x, y, z] | { panel, vertex }

parameters.name: o
parameters.type: { mode?: 'round' | 'chamfer'; radius?: Num | string; distance?: Num | string; size?: Num | string }

properties.name: mode
properties.description: 'round' (default) | 'chamfer'

properties.name: radius
properties.description: fillet radius in mm (mode round)

properties.name: distance
properties.description: chamfer distance in mm (mode chamfer)

properties.name: size
properties.description: radius or distance in mm, for either mode

methods.summary: Cut closed sketch regions out of the sheet, across bends too.
methods.description: Adds a sheetCut from the last sketch (which it consumes). The sketch is read in the FLAT layout: draw it on the plane of the base (or parallel), in flat coordinates. A region is subtracted from every panel it meets and from the flat pattern, so a slot across a bend shows in the DXF; the bend solid loses the matching wedge. Refused if a region misses the sheet, removes or splits a panel, or has an island. Use it instead of a plain cut, which breaks the sheet.

properties.name: regions
properties.description: which sketch regions to cut, as for extrude (default: all)

methods.signature: .sheetRules(o: { name?: string; thickness?: Num | string; kFactor?: Num | string; bendRadius?: Num | string; reliefWidth?: Num | string; reliefDepth?: Num | string; cornerRelief?: Num | string; cornerReliefShape?: 'notch' | 'round' | 'rectangular' | 'tear'; hemGap?: Num | string; gap?: Num | string; active?: boolean } = {})
methods.summary: Sheet stock rule: thickness, k-factor, bend radius.
methods.description: Adds a sheetRules feature. The rule named by baseFlange (or the active rule, the latest one) gives the part its thickness and the bend arithmetic (bend allowance BA = (r + k t) angle). Lengths in mm; any value may be an expression string such as "=Thickness*4" (Thickness is this rule's thickness) or a number with a unit ("2 mm"). Defaults follow the thickness (2.5 when none is given): bendRadius = thickness, kFactor 0.44, reliefWidth = thickness, reliefDepth = thickness / 2, cornerRelief = 4 x thickness, gap = thickness, hemGap 0.01. Put it before the sketch of the base flange.

parameters.name: o
parameters.type: { name?: string; thickness?: Num | string; kFactor?: Num | string; bendRadius?: Num | string; reliefWidth?: Num | string; reliefDepth?: Num | string; cornerRelief?: Num | string; cornerReliefShape?: 'notch' | 'round' | 'rectangular' | 'tear'; hemGap?: Num | string; gap?: Num | string; active?: boolean }

properties.name: name
properties.description: rule name (a rule with an existing name replaces it); baseFlange({ rule }) names it

properties.name: thickness
properties.description: stock thickness in mm (default 2.5)

properties.name: kFactor
properties.description: neutral line position 0..1 (default 0.44)

properties.name: bendRadius
properties.description: default inside bend radius in mm (default = thickness)

properties.name: reliefWidth
properties.description: bend relief width in mm (default = thickness)

properties.name: reliefDepth
properties.description: bend relief depth in mm (default thickness / 2)

properties.name: cornerRelief
properties.description: corner relief size in mm (default 4 x thickness)

properties.name: cornerReliefShape
properties.description: 'notch' (default) | 'round' | 'rectangular' | 'tear'; the others are stored but built as notch for now

properties.name: hemGap
properties.description: default inside radius of a hem in mm (default 0.01)

properties.name: gap
properties.description: gap between the legs of flanges on neighbouring edges made in one feature, mm (default = thickness)

properties.name: active
properties.description: make this the rule of the next base flange (default true)

methods.example:
part('Tray').sheetRules({ name: 'Steel2', thickness: 2, kFactor: 0.44, bendRadius: 2 })
  .sketch('front', (s) => s.rect(100, 60)).baseFlange({ rule: 'Steel2' });

methods.summary: Hollow the body to a wall thickness, opening the selected face(s).
methods.description: Hollows out the solid leaving walls of `thickness` mm and removing the selected face to make an opening (box open at the top: shell(face('>Z'), 2)). faces(...) opens several faces at once. Do fillets of the outside edges before the shell. A thickness larger than the smallest feature fails (shellTooThick).

parameters.name: open
parameters.description: face(sel) or faces(sel) of the face(s) left open

methods.notes:
- Fillet or chamfer the OUTSIDE edges before shelling; shelling a rounded box keeps even walls.
- The selected face is REMOVED (the opening). To close the box again sketch a lid on the rim face and extrude it (recipe hollow-box-lid).
- A thickness that is too big gives shellTooThick / shellFailed with maxThickness in the error.

methods.signature: .sweep(profile: SketchSpec, path: SketchSpec, o: { twist?: Num; op?: 'add' | 'cut'; newBody?: boolean | string; from?: string | string[] } = {})
methods.summary: Sweep a closed profile along a path sketch (pipes, rails, handles).
methods.description: Builds the profile sketch and the path sketch and sweeps the profile along the path. The profile must lie in a plane that the path starts on and is perpendicular to (a circle on 'front' for a path leaving the origin along +Z, which a path sketch on 'right' or 'top' draws as a line in its y or x direction). The path can be a line chain, arcs or a spline. twist turns the profile by that many degrees over the path; op 'cut' removes the swept volume. The kernel has no keep-normal option: the profile follows the path frame.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: path sketch { on, draw } (open chain starting on the profile plane)

parameters.name: o
parameters.type: { twist?: Num; op?: 'add' | 'cut'; newBody?: boolean | string; from?: string | string[] }

properties.name: twist
properties.description: total twist in degrees over the path

properties.name: op
properties.description: 'add' (default) or 'cut'

properties.name: newBody
properties.description: true or 'Name': keep the swept solid as a separate body instead of fusing it with what it touches

properties.name: from
properties.description: with op 'cut': a body name or list of names the cut changes; the other bodies stay as they are

methods.notes:
- The profile plane must be perpendicular to the path where the path starts: a circle on 'front' (normal Z) with a path on 'right' starting along -Z (sketch x of 'right' is -Z), or a path on 'top'. Otherwise sweepProfileNotNormal.
- Profile and path are { on, draw } objects (the sketches are built for you); the profile is closed, the path an open chain starting at the profile plane. Two nested circles make a pipe wall.
- A bend made of lines has sharp corners: for a smooth elbow use arc3 / spline in the path (volume = area x length, Pappus for arcs).
- There is no keep-normal option; twist is the total angle in degrees.

methods.summary: Make the previous extrude or revolve a thin-walled one.
methods.description: Edits the step recorded just before it: the same as passing the thin option. Closed profile gives a hollow section of this wall thickness (centred on the profile).

methods.signature: .thread(on: string, o: { size?: string; diameter?: number; pitch?: number; length?: Num; standard?: string; hand?: 'right' | 'left'; modeled?: boolean })
methods.summary: Add a cosmetic or modeled screw thread to a bore or cylinder.
methods.description: Threads the wall of the bore drilled last (default 'hole'), or a cylinder named by a persistent face name ('F2.S.c1') or 'last:c1' (the c1 face of the last feature, e.g. an extruded circle shaft). Give the designation as size ('M6', 'M12x1.5', '1/4-20') or diameter (+ pitch). Cosmetic by default: no geometry change, the thread is reported in the regen threads list. modeled: true cuts the real helical groove (slow, falls back to cosmetic with a warning). The bore should be the tap drill of the size: the tapped kind of hole() sets that for you.

parameters.name: on
parameters.description: "hole" for the last hole drilled; a face name string; or 'last:<tag>'

parameters.name: o
parameters.type: { size?: string; diameter?: number; pitch?: number; length?: Num; standard?: string; hand?: 'right' | 'left'; modeled?: boolean }

properties.name: size
properties.description: designation, e.g. 'M6' or 'M12x1.5'

properties.name: diameter
properties.description: major diameter in mm (alternative to size)

properties.name: pitch
properties.description: pitch in mm with diameter (fine pitch)

properties.name: length
properties.description: thread length in mm, default the whole face

properties.name: standard
properties.description: 'metric' (default), 'metric-fine', 'UNC', ... (inferred from the size when omitted)

properties.name: hand
properties.description: 'right' (default) | 'left'

properties.name: modeled
properties.description: cut the helical groove

methods.notes:
- Cosmetic by default: the geometry does not change, the thread appears in the regen threads list and drawings. modeled: true cuts the helix; it may fall back to cosmetic with a threadModelFallback warning.
- The hole should be the tap drill of the thread (M6 -> 5.0): hole(..., { kind: 'tapped', thread: 'M6' }) does both. A mismatch is the warning threadDiameterMismatch with the diameter to drill.
- on: 'hole' means the last hole feature (all its positions); a face name must be the persistent name of a cylindrical face.

methods.summary: Unfold the sheet to its flat body.
methods.description: Adds an unfold directly after the sheet features. The body becomes the flat sheet (the flat pattern extruded by the thickness); while unfolded, flanges, hems and folds are refused until refold. The flat pattern itself (outline, bend lines) is always available from sheet_info, folded or not; unfold is for exporting or checking the flat solid.

methods.summary: A flat or split spring washer as its own body, placed by an origin and an axis.
methods.description: kind 'flat' (default) is a ring with the given inner and outer diameter and thickness. kind 'spring' is the same ring split by a straight gap of width `gap` (default the thickness) on the +X side of the placement frame; it is flat (no lift). origin is the centre of the washer's first side and the thickness runs from it along axis (default [0, 0, -1], so a washer at a screw's origin lies under its head, around the shank). The washer does not merge with what it touches. For standard sizes (ISO 7089, ISO 7093-1, DIN 127 B) see the Washer wizard in the app.

parameters.name: o
parameters.description: options object { kind, inner, outer, thickness, gap, origin, axis, name }, the fields below

methods.example:
part('Plate').sketch('front', (s) => s.rect(30, 30)).extrude(4)
  .washer({ inner: 8.4, outer: 16, thickness: 1.6, origin: [0, 0, 4], axis: [0, 0, 1] });

methods.summary: A screw or bolt as its own body (head, drive, shank), placed by an origin and an axis.
methods.description: The free-function form of part.screw: screw({ size: 'M3', length: 6, head: 'button', drive: 'hex' }) adds a screw to the current model and returns it. Sizes M2 to M16 fill in the head and drive; heads pan, button, countersunk, cheese, hex; drives slotted, hex, cross, torx, none. Cross and Torx are approximations. origin is the centre of the bearing face and axis the way the shank points (default [0, 0, -1]); thread: true is refused for now.
methods.example: screw({ size: 'M3', length: 8, head: 'pan', drive: 'cross', origin: [10, 0, 5], axis: [0, 0, -1] });

methods.summary: End condition for cut(): through all material.
methods.description: through() is passed to cut() instead of a depth to cut all the way through the body, in the direction the cut goes (against the sketch normal).

methods.summary: A flat or split spring washer as its own body, placed by an origin and an axis.
methods.description: The free-function form of part.washer: washer({ inner: 8.4, outer: 16, thickness: 1.6 }) adds a flat washer to the current model (a new part when there is none) and returns it. kind: 'spring' splits it with a straight gap of width `gap` (no lift). The thickness runs from the centre `origin` along `axis` (default [0, 0, -1], so a washer at a screw's origin lies under its head).
methods.example: washer({ inner: 8.4, outer: 16, thickness: 1.6, origin: [0, 0, 4], axis: [0, 0, 1] });

methods.summary: Select edges of the current body by direction, extreme plane, or a rule object.
methods.description: edges(sel) is resolved against the body just before the step that uses it. Strings: 'all'; '|X' '|Y' '|Z' straight edges parallel to that axis; '>X' ... '<Z' edges lying in the extreme plane along that axis. A rule object ANDs its keys: parallel ('X'|'Y'|'Z'), outside / inside (box [[x0,y0,z0],[x1,y1,z1]] tested on the edge midpoint), not (another edges()), onFace (a face() or faces()), createdBy (edges that bound a face a feature created: a handle or id), lengthGreater, lengthLess, near + within (radius), and union / intersect / difference (arrays of edges()). It fails with a line number when nothing matches. Choose by POSITION, not by generated names: .sortBy(key) orders the edges by midpoint along key ('>Z' highest first, '<Z' or 'Z' lowest first, likewise X and Y, a direction [x, y, z], or { along: edges(...) } for the distance along a rail edge from its start, the rail being one edge), then .nth(i) (0 first, -1 last), .first(n) and .last(n) take edges in that order: edges({ parallel: 'Y' }).sortBy({ along: edges('|X') }).nth(2) is the third rung along the rail. .groupBy(key, { tol }) gathers the edges at the same position (tol default 0.001 mm) and .nth(i) / .first() / .last() / .at(position) choose a group: edges({ parallel: 'X' }).groupBy('>Z').first() is the edges of the top height, edges('all').groupBy('Z').at(12) those at height 12. Ties are broken by x, y, z, so the choice does not depend on the order the kernel lists edges in, and it is made again when the model is rebuilt. Rule keys sortBy, group and pick do the same in an object. Picking without sortBy or groupBy is refused.

parameters.name: sel
parameters.description: a selector string, or an EdgeRule object

methods.notes:
- Rule keys AND together; use union / intersect / difference for combinations.
- edges('>Z') selects edges lying in the highest plane only (after a boss, that is the boss rim). Combine with onFace or not to refine.
- A selector that matches nothing is an error with the script line, not a silent no-op.

methods.signature: face(sel: string | FaceRule, opts: { of?: FeatureRefLike } = {}): FaceSel
methods.summary: Select ONE face of the current body: by direction, by persistent name, by feature, or by a rule.
methods.description: face(sel, opts) is resolved when the script runs, against the body as it is just before the step that uses it. A direction '>X' '<X' '>Y' '<Y' '>Z' '<Z' ('#top' '#bottom') is the planar face whose outward normal is that axis and which lies furthest along it (ties: the biggest). AFTER A BOSS OR POCKET '>Z' means the boss top, and the plate top facing the same way is a different face: when other faces face the same way but belong to another feature, the run result carries a warning naming the face it resolved to; pick on purpose with face('>Z', { of: handle }) (only faces created by that feature: a handle from part.handle(), or an id like 'F2'). A persistent face name such as 'F3.C1' (cap 1 of F3) selects exactly that face; 'F3.*' is a prefix. A rule object ANDs its keys: dir, normal [x,y,z] (planar faces facing that way), planar, at [x,y,z] (planar: the point lies on its plane), kind ('plane'|'cylinder'|'sphere'|'other'), radius, createdBy / of (feature), areaGreater, areaLess, near [x,y,z] (+ within), not / union / intersect / difference (arrays of face() or faces()). It must match exactly one face (faces(rule).nth(i), .largest(), .smallest(), .near(p) choose among several); it fails with a line number otherwise. Pass it to sketch(), at(), hole(), holes.*, shell().

parameters.name: sel
parameters.description: '>X' '<X' '>Y' '<Y' '>Z' '<Z' '#top' '#bottom', a face name ('F3.C1'), or a FaceRule object

parameters.name: opts
parameters.description: { of: feature handle or id } restrict to the faces that feature created

methods.example:
part('Plate').sketch('front', (s) => s.rect(60, 40)).extrude(10)
  .sketch(face('>Z'), (s) => s.circle(12)).extrude(15)
  .hole(face('>Z'), [0, 0], { diameter: 8 })
  .hole(face('>Z', { of: 'F2' }), [25, 0], { diameter: 5 });
methods.notes:
- A direction ('>Z') matches planar faces by outward normal, the furthest first, ties to the biggest. After a boss or a pocket several faces face the same way: the run result then carries a WARNING naming the face it resolved to and the others. Read warnings; choose on purpose with face('>Z', { of: handle }) (handle = part.handle() right after the feature) or a face name.
- Persistent names ('F3.C1' = cap 1 of F3, 'F3.S.e2' = side of sketch entity e2, 'F8.C0@F10.1' = pattern copy) survive edits that keep the feature; list them with `await part.faces()`.
- A rule object must match exactly ONE face; for several use faces(rule) and .nth(i) / .largest() / .smallest() / .near([x,y,z]).
- Resolved against the body as it is just before the step: after a boss on top, face('>Z') is the boss top, not the plate top.

methods.signature: faces(sel: string | FaceRule, opts: { of?: FeatureRefLike } = {}): FacesSel
methods.summary: Select SEVERAL faces (a set) of the current body, or choose one of them by order, size or position.
methods.description: faces(sel, opts) takes the same specs as face() but returns every match: faces({ kind: 'cylinder', radius: 5 }) is every R5 cylindrical face, faces({ createdBy: h }) every face a feature created, faces('>Z') every face facing +Z. Use it where several faces are wanted (shell(faces(...), t) opens them all, edges({ onFace: faces(...) })), or chain one pick: .nth(i) (position in the body's face list), .largest(), .smallest(), .first(), .last(), .near([x, y, z]) (centroid nearest the point); each returns a face() you can pass to sketch() or hole(). To choose by POSITION instead of by the body's face order (which changes when the model is rebuilt): .sortBy(key) orders the faces by centroid along key ('>Z' highest first, '<Z' or 'Z' lowest first, likewise X and Y, a direction [x, y, z], or { along: edges(...) } for the distance along a rail edge), then .nth(i) / .first() / .last() count in that order: faces({ normal: [0, 0, 1] }).sortBy('Z').nth(1) is the second face facing up from the bottom. .groupBy(key, { tol }) gathers the faces at the same position (default tol 0.001 mm) and .nth(i) / .first() / .last() / .at(position) choose a group, returned as faces(): faces({ normal: [0, 0, 1] }).groupBy('Z').at(18) is every upward face at height 18. Rule keys sortBy and group do the same in an object.

parameters.name: sel
parameters.description: a direction, a face name or prefix ('F3.*'), or a FaceRule (see face)

parameters.name: opts
parameters.description: { of: feature handle or id } restrict to the faces that feature created

methods.example:
part('Block').sketch('front', (s) => s.rect(40, 30)).extrude(20)
  .sketch(face('>Z'), (s) => s.circle(6)).cut(through())
  .fillet(edges({ onFace: faces({ kind: 'cylinder', radius: 6 }) }), 1)
  .shell(faces('<Z').largest(), 2);
methods.notes:
- .nth(i) counts in the body's face list order (stable for one script, not geometric). Prefer .largest(), .smallest(), .near(point) or a rule that pins the face.
- kind and radius come from the display mesh (radius within 0.2 percent); cone and torus faces are kind 'other' for selection (part.faces() read-back reports the kernel's exact surface type).
- shell(faces(...), t) opens several faces at once; edges({ onFace: faces(...) }) takes the edges of any of them.

methods.signature: .hole(on: FaceSel, at: Pt, o: HoleOpts): this
methods.summary: A simple drilled hole on a planar face at [x, y].
methods.description: Drills a round hole into the material from the face. kind selects the shape: 'simple' (default), 'cbore' (counterbore: cboreDiameter and cboreDepth), 'csk' (countersink: cskDiameter, cskAngle default 90) or 'tapped' (thread: 'M6' drills the tap drill and adds the thread; modeled: true for the real helix). size: 'M6' + fit instead of diameter uses the ISO table. end: 'upTo' drills to the next face. [x, y] are coordinates in the sketch plane of that face, measured from the part origin projected onto it (not from a corner). Through unless depth is given. Use flip: true if it cuts the wrong way on an unusual face. Diameter, not radius.

parameters.name: on
parameters.description: face(sel) of the planar face to drill from

parameters.name: at
parameters.description: [x, y] hole centre in the face sketch plane

properties.name: diameter
properties.description: hole diameter in mm

properties.name: kind
properties.description: 'cbore' counterbore (cboreDiameter, cboreDepth), 'csk' countersink (cskDiameter, cskAngle) or 'tapped' (thread: 'M6')

properties.name: depth
properties.description: blind depth in mm, omit for through

properties.name: flip
properties.description: reverse the drilling direction

properties.name: thread
properties.type: string | boolean | { size?: string; length?: Num; hand?: 'right' | 'left'; modeled?: boolean; class?: string }

methods.notes:
- diameter, not radius (circle() is radius). Centres are in the face sketch plane relative to the world origin projected on the face, NOT a corner of the face: a hole at [0, 0] on a plate centred on the origin is in the middle.
- face('>Z') must exist as a planar face at that step. After a shell or fillet on the top, the top face may be a different face: select again.
- Through unless depth is given. Many holes: use holes.points / polar / grid (one feature).
- kind: 'cbore' (counterbore), 'csk' (countersink) and 'tapped' are cut by the kernel only for a STANDARD size: give size: 'M6' (hole diameter 6.6 at the normal fit, ISO 4762 counterbore 11 x 6.4, ISO 10642 countersink 12.4) or a diameter that is a standard clearance hole (6.6 -> M6). A plain 7.3 with kind: 'cbore' is an error that lists the sizes. Override the head with cboreDiameter and cboreDepth TOGETHER, or cskDiameter / cskAngle (default 90).
- kind: 'tapped' with thread: 'M6' drills the tap drill (5.0 for M6) and adds a thread feature on the wall (cosmetic; modeled: true cuts the helix, slow, falls back with a warning). Only metric ISO sizes M2..M24; for other standards drill with diameter and call .thread('hole', { size: '1/4-20' }).
- end: 'upTo' drills to the next face; a blind end needs depth.

methods.summary: Repeat features around an axis.
methods.description: circularPattern(o) repeats the feature added just before it; circularPattern(seed, o) repeats seed ('last', a handle, a feature id, or an array). Instances: count in total over angle (alias total) degrees, 360 = a full circle. axis is 'x' | 'y' | 'z', [ox, oy, oz, dx, dy, dz] or a straight edge; the kernel rotates about a WORLD axis through the origin only, so an offset or oblique axis fails with a clear error (centre the part on the axis, or use holes.polar for a bolt circle anywhere). equalSpacing (default true for 360) spaces the instances angle / count apart; false spaces them angle / (count - 1) so the last lands exactly at the end angle (use it for an arc fan). A pattern can seed another pattern.

parameters.name: seed
parameters.description: 'last', a handle, a feature id or an array of them (omit to repeat the last feature)

properties.name: count
properties.description: total instances

properties.name: axis
properties.description: 'x' | 'y' | 'z' | [ox,oy,oz,dx,dy,dz] | edges(...), default 'z'

properties.name: angle
properties.description: total angle in degrees, default 360 (alias total)

properties.name: equalSpacing
properties.description: angle / count apart (default when 360); false: angle / (count - 1)

properties.name: reverse
properties.description: go the other way

methods.notes:
- The axis is a WORLD axis through the origin (x, y, z, [0,0,0,dx,dy,dz] or a straight edge lying on one); an offset axis is refused with a Line N error. Centre the part on it, or use holes.polar for a bolt circle at any centre.
- equalSpacing (default for 360) steps angle / count; set it false with a partial angle to put the last copy exactly at the end angle.
- Several features: pass an array of handles as the first argument.

methods.summary: Repeat features along a direction, optionally as a 2D grid.
methods.description: linearPattern(o) repeats the feature added just before it; linearPattern(seed, o) repeats seed: 'last', a handle from part.handle(), a feature id like 'F4', or an array of those (several features are patterned together). Instances: count in total (including the original), then ONE of: spacing mm between neighbours; totalLength mm from the first to the last (the kernel keeps the length when the count changes); or to: an object the last copy reaches, measured from the middle of what is patterned: 'front' | 'top' | 'right', at(plane, offset), a flat face(sel) square to the direction, or a point [x, y, z]; toOffset moves that end the way the copies go (negative stops short). The object gives the side, so reverse is not read with to. direction (or axis) is 'x' | 'y' | 'z', a vector [x, y, z] or a straight edge: the kernel patterns along the WORLD axes only, so a vector or edge must be parallel to x, y or z (its sign picks the way); anything oblique fails with a clear error. reverse flips the way. second: { direction, count, spacing | totalLength | to, toOffset?, reverse? } adds a second direction to the same pattern feature: count x second.count instances, a rectangular grid. A run carries the kernel's warnings when copies miss the body (patternCopiesNoEffect), stand apart from it (patternCopiesApart) or overlap each other (patternCopiesOverlap).

parameters.name: seed
parameters.description: 'last', a handle, a feature id or an array of them (omit to repeat the last feature)

properties.name: second
properties.description: { direction, count, spacing | totalLength | to, toOffset?, reverse? } the second grid direction

methods.notes:
- count includes the original; give ONE of spacing (between instances, mm), totalLength (first to last; kept when count changes) or to (the last copy reaches a plane, at(), a flat face(sel) square to the direction, or a point [x,y,z]; toOffset negative stops short).
- The kernel patterns along WORLD x, y or z only: a vector or an edge must be parallel to an axis. Oblique directions are refused with a Line N error.
- Several features: pass an array of handles ([a, b]) as the first argument. A 2D grid is `second: { direction, count, spacing | totalLength | to }` (one feature).
- Warnings `patternCopiesNoEffect` / `patternCopiesApart` / `patternCopiesOverlap` in the run result name copies that miss the body, stand alone, or overlap: fix the spacing or count.
- To pattern a pattern yourself seed with [original, patternHandle].
- A pattern can seed another pattern; the grid helper seeds the second pattern with the originals plus the first pattern (a pattern alone omits its own original).
- Prefer holes.grid when the repeated thing is only drilled holes.

methods.signature: .mirror(plane: Plane | OffsetPlane | FaceSel, o: { body?: boolean } = {})
methods.summary: Mirror the last feature (or the whole body) about a plane.
methods.description: Adds a mirrored copy about 'front' | 'top' | 'right', at(plane, offset) or a planar face(sel). By default the feature added just before (a boss, pocket, hole) is mirrored; with body: true the whole body is reflected and united with the original. The kernel always keeps the original, there is no move-only mirror. Mirror about a face only when the face is the symmetry plane (a face you sketch on is usually not).

properties.name: body
properties.description: mirror the whole body instead of the last feature

methods.notes:
- Without body: true only the feature added just before is mirrored (a boss, pocket, hole); with body: true the whole body is reflected and united with the original.
- The kernel always keeps the original: keepOriginal: false is an error, not a silent no-op.
- The plane is the symmetry plane through the world origin ('right' = YZ, 'top' = XZ, 'front' = XY) or at(plane, offset). Design the half on one side of that plane so the copy lands on the other.

methods.summary: Repeat features along a path sketch, moved or turned with it.
methods.description: pathPattern(o) repeats the feature added just before it; pathPattern(seed, o) repeats seed ('last', a handle, a feature id, or an array). path is a sketch { on, draw } holding an open chain of lines and arcs (as a sweep path). The pattern runs from the path's end nearest the seed; flip runs it from the other end. The seed sits start mm along the path (or startFraction of its length, 0 to 1; default 0) and copy k sits start + k x spacing along it; totalLength instead of spacing spreads the copies first to last. orientation 'fixed' (default) moves the copies without turning them; 'tangent' turns them with the path (round an arc they turn about its centre). A last copy past the end of the path is the error patternBeyondPath, whose maxSpacing is the largest spacing that fits.

parameters.description: 'last', a handle, a feature id or an array of them (omit to repeat the last feature)

properties.name: path
